title: Natural language processing
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how computers process human language: text normalization and tokenization including byte-pair encoding, n-gram language models and smoothing, perplexity, word embeddings, text classification with naive Bayes and logistic regression, sequence labeling, neural language models and transformers for language, pretraining objectives, decoding strategies, evaluation with automatic metrics and human judgment, and bias, multilinguality and the limits of language technology.
primary_reading: Speech and Language Processing by Jurafsky and Martin, 3rd edition draft (free)

weeks.5: Word embeddings: co-occurrence, PMI and word2vec
weeks.6: Text classification with naive Bayes and logistic regression
weeks.7: Sequence labeling: part-of-speech tagging and named entities
weeks.8: Neural language models and transformers for language
weeks.9: Pretraining objectives: masked and causal language modeling
weeks.10: Decoding: greedy search, beam search and sampling
weeks.11: Evaluating generated text: BLEU, ROUGE and human judgment
weeks.12: Bias, multilinguality and the limits of language technology

blocks.deliverable: Train a byte-pair encoder on a small corpus by hand and in code.
Build a bigram model with add-one smoothing and compute its perplexity.
Compute cosine similarities and classify short texts.
Week 7 midterm; tag a sentence with a Viterbi decoder.
Implement greedy, beam and top-k decoding on a toy model.
Audit a small model's outputs for one kind of bias.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Language model and classifier: build a byte-pair tokenizer and a smoothed n-gram language model on a supplied public-domain text, generate text with two decoding strategies, train a naive Bayes classifier on a supplied labeled set of short texts, and write a report with perplexities, sample outputs, error analysis and a section on limitations.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
